intro: Statistics computed automatically from one camera on the sideline. The two teams are recognised by their jersey colour and keep their names when they change ends.
videoCaption: Click a rally to watch it. Beside the video, a top view of the court follows the play.
replayCaption: Click a rally to watch it again on a top view of the court: the players and the ball follow the play.
replayLabel: Top view of the court with the players and the ball, in sync with the video
replayNote: The ball's height is unknown, so its path between two touches is approximate.
noPlayers: Player positions are not available for this match.
watchRally: Watch this rally, then the next ones
noRallies: No rally was found in this video.

captions.contacts: Each dot is a touch of the ball, where it was played, in its team's colour. Click a dot to watch it.
captions.zones: Share of the touches in each zone of each half. Click a zone to watch its touches.
captions.directions: Where each serve and attack went: from the player to the next touch, or to the ball on the floor. Click a flight to watch it.

notes.contacts: Each touch is placed at the feet of the player who played it, or of the player closest under the ball when that player is unknown. A ball on the floor is placed exactly.
notes.zones: Zones are numbered from each team's own end line: 1 back right, 2 front right, 3 front middle, 4 front left, 5 back left, 6 back middle. Touches outside the court count in the nearest zone.
notes.directions: Point: the ball landed in the other court. Error: out, on its own side or in the net. Each flight starts at the player who served or attacked and points to where the ball went; point at one to follow it alone.

emptyDirections: Pick serves or attacks, or all actions, to see where they went.
timelineCaption: Each bar is a rally along the video, taller when longer. Click a bar to watch it.
histCaption: Rallies by number of touches. Click a bar to watch them.
introSides: Statistics computed automatically from one camera on the sideline. Left and right are the two halves of the court as the camera sees them: teams are only recognised with player tracking (the --players option).
numbersNote: Each number is the same player for the whole match, until the players are named.
numbersNoteNamed: Each number is the same player for the whole match; hover over it to see their name.
sidesSet: Seen from the camera, each team on the half it played on.
scoreHint: Worked out from how each rally ends: it can be a point off when a rally was missed.
sidesMixed: Seen from the camera, where each touch was played: the teams change ends between sets, so each half shows both teams' touches.

review.title: Check the players
review.intro: Tracking is unsure about these players: say who is outlined in yellow. Each answer fixes the numbers for the whole match; the questions that matter most come first.
review.oddMark: Not the same person as the other pictures
review.oddHint: A picture shows someone else? Click it, then say who it is if you know. It will be split from this player.
review.moreHint: These pictures look like {{name}}. Click those showing someone else, then confirm: the others will be {{name}}. More pictures follow.
review.moreNone: No more pictures look like them.
review.error: The answer was not saved: is the review server still running?
review.mergeQuestion: Are no. {{a}} and no. {{b}} the same person?
review.video: Video of the moment to check
review.pieceNote: The moment loops, without sound. Player numbers are the tracking's, not the jerseys'.
review.mergeNote: These two players are never on court at the same time: they may be one person, tracked in two pieces.
review.cutWhere: That moment is outside the outlined piece: click while the yellow frame shows (the yellow part under the video). Slow the video down if needed.
review.cutDone: Cut at {{at}}: the two pieces become two players once applied.
review.cutNote: Does the outlined person change midway? Click “The person changes here” (or C) at that moment, the video playing or paused; slow it down if needed. The two parts will be two players.
review.conflictNote: Your answers link them: a piece most likely shows both. Pause the video when the person changes and cut, or forget the answer if it was wrong, then apply.
review.conflictApply: Apply your answers to part them.
review.conflictMarks: Pictures marked as someone else, given to one of them:
review.claimMarks: Pictures marked in a card, and who you said they were:
review.diagnose: Look at the piece's pictures. Two people? The tracking switched players midway: cut (✂) between the last picture of one and the first of the other. One person only? One of your answers is wrong: forget the one that doesn't match the picture.
review.claimSplit: Your answers give this piece ({{from}} – {{to}}) to several people: each picture is likely right, but the tracking switched players midway. Cut (✂) between them.
review.moments: Your other answers in this piece (click to see the moment):
review.pinned: All your answers giving a piece to {{names}}
review.pinnedNote: Given while these players were joined, they may sit under the wrong name. If the picture doesn't show the person named, pick who it is: the answer is corrected.
review.mergeWarn: Careful: this answer would join {{names}}, who carry different names, into one player. Save it anyway?
review.doneApply: Apply your answers to update the match page. More questions may follow, fewer each time.
review.doneNothing: Tracking has no doubt left that matters: the others each concern under 10 seconds of play.
review.namesIntro: Give each player a name: the match page shows it instead of their number. The jersey number is optional. Giving two numbers the same name makes them one player. Each name is saved when you leave its box; apply them to update the page. The Questions tab then fixes the players tracking is unsure about. Keyboard: ↑ ↓ move between players, ← → between pictures, Space marks the picture (type the name, Enter), N names the player.
review.name: Name
review.sameName: Same name as {{players}}: they will become one player. For two different people, add the initial of the surname.
review.applyBoth: Apply the answers and the names
review.touchQuestion: Who touches the ball in the yellow frame?
review.touchNote: Only the slow-motion part counts, while the yellow frame shows. If nobody touches the ball during it, answer "Nobody".
review.aceQuestion: Who misses the reception of this serve?
review.aceNote: The serve plays in slow motion until it lands. Pick the player of the receiving team who should have taken it; if it lands out of everyone's reach, answer "Nobody".

touchWhy.twice: the same player twice in a row
touchWhy.close: two players as near the ball

review.nobody: Nobody touches it in the frame
review.rallyNote: The moment plays whole, unzoomed. A rally runs from the serve to the end of the point; the warm-up, a ball sent back to the server or a timeout are none.
review.hostedFailed: The online page could not be updated at {{at}}: your answers are applied here, try again later.

loopVideo: Loop (replays the rally or moment playing)
noRally: No rally found in the video.

about.touches: Every time the player touches the ball, whatever the action.
about.serves: The serves, which put the ball in play.
about.aces: The serves that land straight in the other court.
about.serveFaults: The serves into the net or out.
about.receptions: The first touches on the other team's serve, aces conceded included.
about.missed: The receptions lost: the ball lands, goes out or into the net. An ace conceded counts against the player nearest to where it landed.
about.unattacked: The receptions after which the team sends the ball back or loses it without attacking.
about.rated: The receptions' mean rating, out of 3, from where the next touch is played: 3 within 1.5 m of the setter's target (1 m off the net, between zones 2 and 3), 2 within 3 m, 1 further or sent straight over the net, 0 for a fault.
about.sets: The team's second touches, the ones that set up the attack.
about.attacks: The third touches, hit above the head to send the ball to the other team.
about.kills: The attacks that land in the other court.
about.attackFaults: The attacks out, into the net or landing on the player's own side.
about.relances: The third touches sent back without attacking, with a forearm or an overhead pass.
about.relanceFaults: The free balls out, into the net or landing on the player's own side.
about.blocks: The balls touched at the net right after the other team's attack.
about.digs: The first touches on the other team's attack or free ball.
about.digFaults: The digs lost: the ball lands, goes out or into the net.
about.unattackedDigs: The digs after which the team sends the ball back or loses it without attacking.
about.points: Balls played that land in the other court.
about.faults: Balls sent out, into the net or landing on the player's own side, aces conceded included.
about.between: Balls that landed untouched within 2.5 m of two teammates about as close as each other. Calling the ball wins them: “Mine!”
about.strengths: What a player does clearly better than the rest of their team, with at least 5 attempts on each side and a 20-point gap. Click one to watch those moments.
about.toWorkOn: What a player does clearly worse than the rest of their team, with at least 5 attempts on each side and a 20-point gap. Click one to watch those moments.
about.time: Time on the court during the rallies (minutes:seconds), from the players' tracking: rough where a player is poorly tracked.

stats.noteTitles: Hover or tap a column's title to see what it counts; click it to sort the rows.
stats.noteVideo: It all comes from the video: touches can be missing or given to the wrong player.

insights.title: Analysis
insights.detail: {{n}} of {{of}} ({{p}}), against {{restN}} of {{restOf}} ({{restP}}) for the rest of the team

players.title: Statistics
players.caption: What each player did with the ball. Click a number to watch those moments again.
players.captionSides: Without player tracking, touches are counted per side of the net, as seen from the camera. Click a number to watch those moments again.
players.noCards: No identified player of this team touched the ball: the table shows the whole team's touches.

cards.mvpWhy: MVP: the best balance per minute played, points won minus faults, of every player of both teams on the court at least half as long as the longest. {{points}} points won (attacks, aces, blocks) for {{faults}} faults in {{time}} played: +{{balance}}.

scene3d.label: Court view
scene3d.note: The camera does not give the ball's height: each flight rises as high as gravity requires for its duration, and each touch sits at a typical height for its action. Drag to turn around the court, pinch or scroll to zoom.

matches.title: Matches
matches.intro: Each match's stats, computed automatically from the video. Pick a match to see its report.

feedback.open: Something wrong in this moment? Report it
feedback.thanks: Thank you! Your report will help correct the analysis.
feedback.failed: It could not be sent: try again in a moment.

kinds.action: It's not the right action (set, attack…)
kinds.result: The result or the point is wrong

videoChoice.title: How to see the match?
videoChoice.text: With the video, for the players and their families: enter the password. Without, the stats and the play replayed on a top view of the court.
videoChoice.changed: The password changed: enter the new one.
